name: Bhargava Narasimha Temple, Ahobilam
deity: Vishnu as Bhargava Narasimha — named for Parashurama (Bhargava Rama), who is said to have done penance here
period: One of the Nava Narasimha shrines of Ahobilam in the Nallamala hills of Andhra Pradesh
summary: On a forested hill beside the Bhargava, or Akshaya, Tirtha near Lower Ahobilam, Bhargava Narasimha honours the penance of Parashurama, the avatar of the Bhrigu line, before the lion-lord.

sections.history: Bhargava Narasimha stands about two kilometres from Lower Ahobilam, on a hill beside a sacred pond known as the Bhargava Tirtha, or Akshaya Tirtha. It is one of the nine Narasimha shrines of Ahobilam, and its name ties it to Parashurama, called Bhargava as a descendant of the sage Bhrigu, who tradition holds performed penance here to behold Narasimha. The shrine is part of the worship of the nine forms cared for by the Ahobila Matha, and its stone structure is generally associated with the Vijayanagara period. Set in thick scrub forest away from the main road, it remains one of the quieter of the nine.
sections.architecture: A short walk from the pond leads to a flight of well over a hundred steep stone steps, at the top of which stands a compact shrine. The image shows Narasimha in the act of slaying Hiranyakashipu, with Prahlada standing nearby with folded hands — the young devotee whose faith set the whole story in motion.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Parashurama, the sixth avatar of Vishnu, came to this hill and performed austerities beside the pond, and that Narasimha revealed himself to him here; hence Bhargava Narasimha, the Lord of the Bhargava. The pond is called Akshaya, inexhaustible, for tradition holds that its water never fails. In the astrological reading of the nine shrines, Bhargava Narasimha is linked with the Sun.
sections.festivals: Narasimha Jayanti and the annual Brahmotsavam of Ahobilam are observed across the nine shrines; many pilgrims bathe in the pond before darshan. Confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: The track from Lower Ahobilam is rough and is usually covered by hired jeep or auto, followed by the stepped climb. It can be hot and exposed by midday, so go early. Older pilgrims often visit Bhargava on a different day from the Upper Ahobilam shrines to spread the effort.

visit.timings: Worship is offered daily; the shrine is reached by a rough track and a stepped climb, best made in the morning. Confirm current timings locally.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Lower Ahobilam is reached by road via Allagadda; Nandyal is the nearest major railhead. The shrine is about two kilometres from Lower Ahobilam by an unpaved track — local jeeps are the usual transport — followed by the steps up the hill.
